doc.title: Joanne Brackeen interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 10, 2001

title: Finding work in 1960s New York: lofts and La Boehme
summary: She says the 60s were innovative; she worked with Blakey, played lofts, and had a six-night club job with Pete LaRoca and Dave Liebman.

bands.name: Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: What’s it like trying to — what year was this now? In the 60s you came here?
I came here in the 60s yeah.
To break in — well the 60s, maybe you can tell me as far as the decades for jazz, the 60s wasn’t one of the healthiest I don’t think.
But as far as finding work, was it hard for you to find work here in New York?
Well I was working with Art Blakey so—
You couldn’t have done much better than that.

There was a lot of loft scenes around, and a lot of just sessions. People — I remember working in a club that didn’t pay anything but somehow I got hooked up with Pete LaRoca Sims and Dave Liebman and there was — if I could remember the name of the club, they’d know, La Boehme. We worked there six nights a week and Dave Holland used to come down. There was a lot of us that just — we would play, we would get paid something but not what you would consider very much. There was a lot of playing going on, innovative playing. People had their own signatures. They had their own, you know, everybody didn’t sound like one person, where we have a tendency now, that a lot of people tend toward that, not that that’s bad.
